title: share what you earn

lines: A BAG OF CHIPS ON THE BUS.
HOLD IT TIGHTER, OR TIP IT OVER?
cards: A kid on the school bus has a bag of chips, and a friend is looking at it. There's a tiny moment where the kid decides: hold it tighter, or tip the bag over and say, want some?
Most of us are still making that decision, just with bigger bags: a paycheck, a spare room, an afternoon. Today, the second pillar.

teach.b: Vand chakna. Vand means to share, to divide into portions. Chakna means to eat, to take your part.
Share, and then eat. Notice the order. Not eat, and share what's left over.
Share first, then enjoy what's yours. Yesterday's line from the scripture praised the one who earns by effort and gives some away with their own hand. Today is that second half.
Your own hand: not a tax, not a charity you've never seen.
Many Sikhs give in a particular way called dasvandh, a tenth: a tenth of what they earn, set aside for others and the community, the langar, the gurdwara, someone in need.

teach.h: EARN CLEAN, THEN LET SOME GO.
teach.b: Some give exactly a tenth, some give what they can, and some give their time instead. And the two pillars lean on each other. Honest work alone could make a hard worker who keeps everything.
Sharing alone could be generous with money that wasn't fairly earned. Together: earn cleanly, then let some of it go. The langar from day two runs on exactly this.

how: Sikhs practice vand chakna by sharing food, time and income with others; many give dasvandh, a tenth of their earnings, to the gurdwara, the langar or people in need.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: to eat, to take your part

s: vand chakna means eat first and share what's left
the order is share, then eat. you give first.
many Sikhs set aside a tenth of what they earn for others and the community.
food, time and skills all count; some give their time instead.

games.q: you've just been paid for honest work. what does the second pillar ask?
o: keep it all. you earned it fairly.
share a portion first, then enjoy the rest.
give it all away and keep nothing.
games.why: vand chakna: share, then eat. the scripture praises the one who earns by effort and gives some with their own hand.

practice: Think about what came into your hands this week: money, food, time, a skill, a kindness. Pick one thing, and picture dividing it, the way you'd tip the bag over. Picture who you'd hand a portion to, and their face when you do.

wordCard.voice: Vand chakna. Share, then eat: dividing what you've earned so others have a portion too. The second pillar. Thirteenth word.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: vand (share, divide) + chhakna (to eat).

carryVoice: Your line: share it first. Not what's left over at the end, but the first portion. Day thirteen.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1245 (earning by effort and giving with one's own hand)
